learningObjective: Diagnose sustained-vs-burst GPU throughput given TDP constraints and identify power capping as a mechanism.

canonicalClaims.claim: Data-center GPUs use DVFS to keep long-run power draw within their TDP cap; sustained throughput can therefore be lower than short-burst throughput on compute-bound kernels because clocks reduce as the die heats up.
conditions: Ambient/system cooling and firmware policies are the standard configuration.
Measurement duration is long enough that TDP-average kicks in.
nonImplications: Does not imply every burst-vs-sustained gap is TDP-driven; other causes exist.
Does not imply memory-bound kernels are equally throttled; HBM traffic is less clock-sensitive.

misconceptions.claim: HBM bandwidth drops under thermal load, causing the sustained throughput drop.
misconceptions.whyWrong: HBM bandwidth is largely thermally stable across normal operating temperatures; the compute-bound throughput drop tracks clock frequency, not memory bandwidth.

misconceptions.claim: Profiler overhead accounts for the 20% burst-vs-sustained gap.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Profiler overhead does not systematically bias short bursts vs sustained runs by 20%; consistent measurements typically capture both phases similarly.

misconceptions.claim: PCIe bandwidth throttles compute under thermal load.
misconceptions.whyWrong: A resident GEMM does not need PCIe traffic during execution; PCIe is only involved for H2D/D2H, not for the kernel's ongoing compute.

implementationFacts: nvidia-smi reports Power Limit, Power Draw, Perf State (P-states), and current SM clocks.
Data-center GPUs (A100, H100) support nvidia-smi -pl to configure power caps within a range.
performanceScenarios: Server-side inference workloads can see 10–20% sustained throughput loss under aggressive power caps, motivating careful capacity planning for LLM serving.
